claims.text: What the strip looks like The main change is a short QT interval.
claims.quote: The main ECG abnormality seen with hypercalcaemia is shortening of the QT interval

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) QT: short
claims.quote: Hypercalcemia: Short QT, short ST segment, Osborn J waves in severe cases

claims.text: ST segment: short
claims.quote: Hypercalcemia: Short QT, short ST segment, Osborn J waves in severe cases

claims.text: J point: Osborn (J) waves in severe cases
claims.quote: Hypercalcemia: Short QT, short ST segment, Osborn J waves in severe cases

claims.text: Rhythm: in severe hypercalcemia arrhythmias may occur, particularly in patients taking digoxin
claims.quote: In severe hypercalcemia, a shortened QTc interval is shown on ECG, and arrhythmias may occur, particularly in patients taking digoxin.

claims.text: Extreme hypercalcemia: ventricular irritability and VF arrest have been reported
claims.quote: Ventricular irritability and VF arrest has been reported with extreme hypercalcaemia

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Most common: hyperparathyroidism and cancer
claims.quote: The most common causes of hypercalcemia are hyperparathyroidism and cancer.

claims.text: Causes: hyperparathyroidism (primary and tertiary), myeloma, bony metastases, paraneoplastic syndromes, milk-alkali syndrome, sarcoidosis, excess vitamin D (e.g., iatrogenic)
claims.quote: Causes of Hypercalcaemia Hyperparathyroidism (primary and tertiary) Myeloma Bony metastases Paraneoplastic syndromes Milk-alkali syndrome Sarcoidosis Excess vitamin D (e.g. iatrogenic)

claims.text: Cancer: a common cause, usually in hospitalized patients; several mechanisms, but the calcium ultimately comes from bone resorption
claims.quote: Cancer is a common cause of hypercalcemia, usually in hospitalized patients. Although there are several mechanisms, elevated serum calcium ultimately occurs as a result of bone resorption.

claims.text: Sarcoidosis: appears to be due to unregulated conversion of 25 hydroxyvitamin D (calcifediol) to 1,25 hydroxyvitamin D (calcitriol)
claims.quote: In sarcoidosis, hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria appear to be due to unregulated conversion of 25 hydroxyvitamin D (calcifediol) to 1,25 hydroxyvitamin D (calcitriol

claims.text: Symptoms Mild hypercalcemia: many patients are asymptomatic
claims.quote: In mild hypercalcemia, many patients are asymptomatic.

claims.text: GI: constipation, anorexia, nausea and vomiting, abdominal pain, and ileus
claims.quote: Clinical manifestations of hypercalcemia include constipation, anorexia, nausea and vomiting, abdominal pain, and ileus.

claims.text: Kidney: impaired concentrating ability → polyuria, nocturia, and polydipsia
claims.quote: Impairment of the renal concentrating mechanism leads to polyuria, nocturia, and polydipsia.

claims.text: Calcium > 12 mg/dL: can cause emotional lability, confusion, delirium, psychosis, stupor, and coma
claims.quote: Elevation of serum calcium > 12 mg/dL (> 3.00 mmol/L) can cause emotional lability, confusion, delirium, psychosis, stupor, and coma.

claims.text: Neuromuscular: may cause skeletal muscle weakness
claims.quote: Hypercalcemia may cause neuromuscular symptoms, including skeletal muscle weakness.

claims.text: Calcium > 18 mg/dL: may cause shock, renal failure, and death
claims.quote: Hypercalcemia > 18 mg/dL (> 4.50 mmol/L) may cause shock, renal failure, and death.

claims.text: Treatment Mild (< 11.5 mg/dL): besides treating the cause, oral phosphate or isotonic saline plus a loop diuretic
claims.quote: In addition to treating the cause, treat mild hypercalcemia (serum calcium < 11.5 mg/dL [< 2.9 mmol/L]) with oral phosphate or isotonic saline plus a loop diuretic.

claims.text: Moderate (> 11.5 and < 18 mg/dL): add a bisphosphonate, corticosteroids, and sometimes calcitonin
claims.quote: For moderate hypercalcemia (serum calcium > 11.5 mg/dL [< 2.9 mmol/L] and < 18 mg/dL [< 4.5 mmol/L]), add a bisphosphonate, corticosteroids, and sometimes calcitonin.

claims.text: Severe: hemodialysis may be needed
claims.quote: For severe hypercalcemia, hemodialysis may be needed.

claims.text: Consider parathyroidectomy for progressive or symptomatic hyperparathyroidism
claims.quote: Consider parathyroidectomy in patients with progressive or symptomatic hyperparathyroidism.
